title: Drawing the line
subtitle: Asahi bans AI code, agents learn to ask first, and a Senate bill makes data centers pay
editor_note: Today is about boundaries. Licences, approvals and private networks each decide who gets in.

sections.headline: Asahi shuts the gate on AI
sections.deck: Asahi Linux relicenses to GPL and forbids generative AI. Omarchy says its patches are now turned away.
sections.art_alt: A dusk fence with one open gap and a warm path of light leading through it
sections.why: A flagship open-source project drew a hard line on AI-written code.

items.headline: Pinky asks before your agent pays
items.why: Open-source phone control that stops for approval before payments and deletes.

items.headline: Hermes reviews code for security bugs
items.why: It verifies each finding and can write a repro in a temporary copy.

items.headline: Codex Pro has no 5-hour limits
items.why: Pro tiers give 10x, 20x or 50x Plus usage, per OpenAI’s Codex lead.

items.headline: OpenAI Devs: “Tomorrow.”
items.why: A one-word video teaser with no details, so expect news today.

items.headline: Omarchy 4.5 installs beside macOS
items.why: A native Mac installer for M1–M3 and MacBook Neo; M4+ not ready.

sections.deck: Who may touch the code, and who decides.

sections.headline: Asahi leaves MIT for the GPL
sections.deck: Lunduke Journal: the change is immediate, aimed at “bad faith actors” who would replace the project and monetize it.
sections.why: Anything built on Asahi’s MIT code now faces a different licence going forward.

sections.headline: Same ban, two reactions
sections.verdict: Both accept the legal risk of tainted clean-room work. They split on whether the ban helps developers or simply closes a door.

items.label: Omarchy (DHH)
items.note: Says Asahi now refuses upstreaming of Omarchy’s Apple Silicon work.

items.label: A developer
items.note: Calls the legal worry fair but rejects “for your own good.”

items.headline: Private networks allow riskier features
items.why: tldraw designs for “high trust networks” where reckless public-web features become safe.

items.headline: pstack adds verification skills
items.why: Formal-verification and statechart skills for modeling state machines and flows.

items.headline: Amp set up a Pi without a login
items.why: Flash, boot and SSH setup handled by the agent; scope the key.

items.headline: DeepSeek Harness: everything is a plugin
items.why: Built-ins can be replaced by third-party plug-ins, like phone-OS apps.

items.headline: Stripe: send a product critique to apply
items.why: Agentic-commerce team got 500+ emails and wants a screenshot plus critique.
